title: Part 1
text: Picture a creature weighing up to two hundred tons, sinking into total darkness. Its death is about to feed a desert.

title: Part 2
text: The real miracle happens when the carcass does not wash up on a beach, but sinks into the open sea. Marine biologists call this a whale fall.
nxt: Many carcasses float for a while, buoyed by the gases of decomposition. Once those gases escape, or if the whale was lean and dense to begin with, the body sinks.

title: Part 3
text: To understand a whale fall, you must understand the deep seafloor. The abyssal plains cover a huge share of our planet, and much of that ground is a biological desert.
nxt: Sunlight never reaches it, temperatures hover near freezing, and the pressure is crushing. Food is scarce.

nxt: Most animals live on marine snow, which is tiny flakes of dead plankton and debris drifting down from above. For this starved world, a whale is a windfall beyond comprehension.

title: Part 4
text: After hours or even days of falling, the whale touches down on the muddy plain. The impact likely kicks up thick clouds of silt.
nxt: In an instant, a flat, barren landscape has gained a mountain of food.

title: Part 5
text: Although the deep ocean seems empty, news travels fast through chemical currents.
nxt: Scent trails from the carcass spread through the cold water, and scavengers with highly sensitive chemical senses can pick them up from far away.
